scenarios.title: Reconcile synthetic interrupted media and expired authorization records
plannedActions: Complete initial service assertions, then configure only the local scheduled-event adapter and reacquire fixture D1/R2 handles.
Provision synthetic owner/session and two teams; create each project through real HTTP. Stage the nine named media states and independently expected object metadata/bytes.
Compare all asset rows, R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata and exact per-team reserved bytes with authored fixture values. Save complete project rows.

Stage expired/live OAuth state, authorization code, email challenge and rate-limit records plus old-expired/recent-expired/revoked-live sessions. Observe stale recoverable media unavailable and preexisting ready media readable.
Capture full expiry tables and define removals by the explicitly authored expired record IDs. Define four expected retained media rows, changing only the matching stale upload to ready.
Invoke one local scheduled event over HTTP and require platform outcome ok; poll only read-only media state for at most 5 seconds.

Compare every final asset row, R2 key/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata and both teams' exact reserved bytes. Compare all expiry tables with the independently named removals and preserve both full project rows.

GET recovered, old-ready and same-digest other-project sentinel media and compare exact bytes/MIME/digest header. Require unavailable responses for the five removed replicas and the retained fresh upload.
Capture expiry state after legitimate public verification reads; invoke the same local scheduled adapter once more.

Require identical media rows/objects/quotas and expiry records, then reread the recovered bytes; keep the original ASSETS bucket empty and require exactly 2 triggers and 0 outbound attempts before awaited cleanup.
expectedOutcomes: One matching stale upload becomes ready; exactly five stale D1 rows and four existing R2 objects are removed, leaving four rows and four objects, and 87 row-reserved bytes are released. Fresh upload, old ready and same-digest other-project/team sentinel retain exact rows, keys, bytes and specified metadata, with unchanged sentinel-team quota. Recovered, old-ready and same-digest other-project media return exact fixture bytes, image/png and their SHA headers. Removed media and the retained nonready fresh upload return 404 asset_unavailable.

Only the named expired OAuth/code/email/rate records and 31-day-old expired session disappear. Live records, recent-expired and revoked-live sessions, prior counters and both project rows remain exact.

Second scheduled invocation preserves the complete retained media/quota/expiry state, recovered media remains exact, original ASSETS stays empty and no outbound attempt occurs. Request counters from verification GETs are captured before the repeat rather than mistaken for cleanup mutation.

associations.rationale: The actual scheduled orchestrator batches the five named cleanup operations and starts media reconciliation; synthetic teams have no Stripe customer so provider reconciliation is excluded. The complete shared contract also checks media outcomes.
